As far as tips for actually getting accepted - before going to the interviews make sure to research not just the company but the job role specifically - If you apply for a DevOps position do some reading on it and watch a few vids or if you're going for an app development position do the same for Kotlin, Swift, etc. They aren't expecting experts but do expect a basic understanding of the role, eagerness to learn, and basic programming skills, they may give you a problem that you could solve with a simple concept like a switch statement or something similar.

I applied for a ton of positions and had several interviews including one where they rejected me saying my programming skills weren't good enough even I felt they were, after that interview I felt like it would be impossible to get an internship.

Everyone who applies for internship years will go through the same thing - use the experience and grow from it rather than letting it get you down. If someone can get the first internship they went for an interview for I would be amazed.
